html:
SMTO-SKL-0054 — Google Drive files can only be moved inside a conversation

GUID: bad3d571-19c4-5a2a-b48d-8a96f546e002
Slug: google-drive-artifact-context-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • To download a file from Google Drive or upload one to it, SMTO keeps the file inside a conversation. This request ran somewhere without one, so SMTO stopped before moving any file.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open SMTO's main conversation view, start or open a conversation, and type your request there, for example "download Budget 2026 from my Google Drive". Downloaded and uploaded files are kept with a conversation, so the request has to come from one.
  2. For an upload, first add the file to that same conversation with Add files to conversation, then ask SMTO to upload it. SMTO only uploads files that belong to the conversation you are in.
  3. If you already asked from a normal conversation, start a new conversation and ask there once more. A new conversation gets its own file area, so this shows whether only the first one was set up wrongly.

What success looks like

  • The downloaded file appears under Artifacts in the conversation, or SMTO confirms the upload with the file's name.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Say where you made the request (a conversation, a Workflow or somewhere else) and that a new conversation didn't help.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Google Drive download, export or upload was attempted without an artifact registry or without a current run and conversation scope in the tool context.

What this means

  • Transfer setup has no artifact registry or lacks current run/conversation ownership. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Transfer setup has no artifact registry or lacks current run/conversation ownership.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect artifact context and run/conversation scope before starting transfer.

How to fix it

  • Run the transfer from a native Agent run, where artifacts.runtime.bind sets _artifact_store and _artifact_scope (run_id and conversation_id) in the tool context. If a normal conversation run still raises this, the run's artifact workspace binding failed; check the Server log for that run.
  • Run the transfer in a conversation with an active artifact workspace.

Retry and execution caution

  • Run the transfer in a conversation with an active artifact workspace.

How to verify the fix

  • The operation runs with a valid owned artifact workspace.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
